qf1-premise.title: Is #690's stated premise still true in the code, and what is the genuine residual defect?
qf1-premise.imperative: The issue asserts sigma_plus = hypot(mu, sigma). Verify against the code AND against unmerged branches touching the same seam. State the residual defect in behaviour terms: what present-tense thing does the system do wrong that this issue must change?
qf1-premise.finding: PARTLY STALE. On main (3541d292) class_utilization_observable.py:122 is still 'return float(math.hypot(mu, sigma))'. BUT unmerged branch fix/721-grip-band-units (commits a5b24249, 9fae4c9d; issue #721 OPEN) already replaces it with 'abs(sigma)' and changes the signature to onesided_sigma_from_grip(sigma), because mu is the ABSOLUTE session pace level (~90s). So #690's headline mechanism -- 'mu is whole-lap pace and must not be in the scale' -- is already fixed on that branch. CODE EVIDENCE: git diff main...fix/721-grip-band-units -- src/physics/utilization/class_utilization_observable.py. RESIDUAL DEFECT (the genuine #690 scope): even with sigma alone, compute_class_utilization_observable:379-385 computes ONE scalar g_sigma_onesided and hands the SAME value to every per-class band, so the (2+k) per-class bands each carry the WHOLE-LAP grip sigma. Since time_deficit_by_class is an exact additive partition of lap_time_deficit_s (class_ledger.py ClassDeficits docstring), the per-class widths sum to (2+k)*sigma_lap instead of sigma_lap -- the band on each part is as wide as the band on the whole. That is the present-tense wrong behaviour #690 must change.

qf2-units-consumers.title: What are get_grip_at's units, and who consumes g_sigma_onesided at what grain?
qf2-units-consumers.imperative: Confirm the unit claim (whole-lap pace seconds) from get_grip_at's own definition. Then enumerate the full consumer topology of g_sigma_onesided per the project's cite-seams-and-consumer-topology planning invariant.
qf2-units-consumers.finding: UNITS CONFIRMED: grip_store.get_grip_at:220-251 returns (mu, sigma) where mu is 'the fitted pace level (session_offset + curve_asymptote*(1-exp(-curve_rate*x)))' -- i.e. WHOLE-LAP pace seconds -- and sigma is the delta-method propagation of that same whole-lap quantity. #690's unit claim is correct. CONSUMER TOPOLOGY of g_sigma_onesided (grep, non-.agent-work): (1) PRODUCER src/physics/utilization/class_utilization_observable.py:339,379,396 (dataclass field + compute). (2) scripts/build_class_utilization_observables.py:462 writes float(obs.g_sigma_onesided) into EVERY per-class DriverClassObservableRow, and :476 logs it. (3) src/physics/utilization/reference_utilization_store.py:78,94,126 -- the persisted column on driver_class_observables. (4) REAL DOWNSTREAM CONSUMER src/physics/fingerprint/fit.py: :111 SELECTs it, :139/:172/:195/:204/:226 aggregates it recency-weighted per (driver, class) cell, :247-257 composes sigma_cell = sqrt(sigma0^2 + shared_floor^2 + g_sigma_onesided^2 + sigma_lapsampling^2), :298 applies it. fit.py filters class LIKE _SEVERITY_CLASS_SQL_PATTERN, so only the corner-severity classes reach it. (5) NOT a consumer: src/physics/utilization/class_utilization_validation.py (grep for sigma/band/grip returns nothing). (6) Docs: docs/architecture/packets/physics.md:1522,1741; docs/physics/season_670_report.md:82,99; scripts/run_heldout_diagnostic_670.py:636. KEY CONSEQUENCE: because fit.py's cell grain is ALREADY (driver, class), a per-class sigma flows through fit.py with NO code change there.

qf3-substrate-schema.title: Does a per-class quantity that can carry the scaling already exist, and does per-class sigma force a schema change?
qf3-substrate-schema.imperative: Look for an existing, structurally-normalised per-class weight in the g1 ledger. Check whether the persisted row grain already admits a per-class sigma value without a column change.
qf3-substrate-schema.finding: SUBSTRATE EXISTS. src/physics/utilization/class_ledger.py already ships ClassTimeLedger.time_share_by_class = time_by_class_s / lap_time_s, shape (2+k), 'Sums to 1.0 by construction (each W row sums to 1)', built by class_time_ledger(segment_map, distance_m, speed). It is dimensionless, structurally normalised, uses ONLY the map geometry and one speed profile (no v_real/v_ideal ratio, so it cannot breach the #628 anti-circularity contract), and is the exact same W-column order as time_deficit_by_class. That is the natural carrier for a per-class scaling weight -- nothing new needs minting. NOTE: class_deficits() returns ClassDeficits which does NOT expose time shares (only speed_deficit/time_deficit/n_points/lap_time_deficit/W), so the observable must either call class_time_ledger separately or ClassDeficits must be extended. SCHEMA: NO column change needed. reference_utilization_store.py _CLASS_COLUMNS already carries g_sigma_onesided on a row whose PK includes 'class' (_CLASS_PK: year, session_type, gp_name, round_idx, constructor, driver, class...) and build_class_utilization_observables.py:449-470 already emits one row PER class. The per-class value simply replaces the repeated scalar in an existing per-class slot.

qd1-base.title: DECISION: which base does #690 build on -- main, or the unmerged fix/721-grip-band-units?
qd1-base.imperative: Block on the counterpart. No human reachable: record the question verbatim, decide it per the dispatch's standing authorisation, and state the consequence of the alternative.
qd1-base.finding: ASKED: 'Issue #721 (OPEN) has an unmerged branch fix/721-grip-band-units that already rewrites the same function -- do I base #690 on it, or on main?' DECIDED (no human reachable; dispatch authorises): BASE ON fix/721-grip-band-units. (a) #690 is only coherent after #721: per-class scaling of hypot(~90s, sigma) would just redistribute a pace level. (b) Both change onesided_sigma_from_grip's SIGNATURE -- basing on main guarantees a manual conflict. (c) #721 already amends three of the same test files. CONSEQUENCE OF THE ALTERNATIVE: #690 would ship a per-class scaling of a quantity #721 deletes. RESIDUAL RISK: if #721 is reworked, #690 rebases -- low, since #721's diagnosis is measured (93/93 curve-fitted sessions still band >10s with offset_sigma forced to zero). If #721 merges before #690 starts, rebase onto main and this decision is a no-op. @grade: settled/measured

qd2-law.title: DECISION: which per-class scaling law -- time-share-linear, sqrt-share, or grip-sensitivity-weighted?
qd2-law.imperative: Block on the counterpart. This is the load-bearing choice the issue's 'documented rationale' acceptance criterion is about. Record the question, the candidates, and the decision.
qd2-law.finding: ASKED: 'What law scales the whole-lap grip sigma down to a per-class band width?' CANDIDATES: (A) time-share-linear sigma_c = s_c*sigma_session; (B) sqrt-share sigma_c = sqrt(s_c)*sigma_session; (C) grip-sensitivity weighting (corners weighted above straights); (D) deficit-proportional. DECIDED (dispatch authorises): (A) TIME-SHARE-LINEAR, weights = ClassTimeLedger.time_share_by_class. RATIONALE (this IS the issue's 'documented rationale' deliverable): grip is a SESSION-LEVEL COMMON-MODE effect -- one fitted curve per (year, gp_name, session_type) -- so it perturbs every class of one lap coherently, not independently. Under perfect correlation, per-part uncertainties add LINEARLY, giving the coherence identity sum_c sigma_c = sigma_session, which exactly mirrors the point-side identity sum_c time_deficit_c = lap_time_deficit_s that ClassDeficits already guarantees. Given normalised weights, linear share-weighting is the UNIQUE law satisfying it. Weight = time share (not n_points share) because the perturbed quantity is TIME (G is a pace-second) and the wrapped location is a transit-TIME deficit; n_points share is a telemetry-grid sampling artifact. REJECTED: (B) is the INDEPENDENT-errors composition (sum sigma_c^2 = sigma^2) -- wrong correlation model, and it over-widens exactly the small classes the bug already hurts most (sqrt(0.05)=0.224 vs 0.05, 4.5x too wide). (D) makes the width depend on the quantity it bounds -- a #628-flavoured circularity. (C) is physically the best but mints a per-class grip weighting module G does not carry: that is 're-fitting G', explicitly out of #690 scope, and the project forbids new physical weightings without L1-L4 truth evidence -> route to triage as a follow-on. @grade: guess . leans g2 . settle: recompute the #670 held-out coverage/log-score under (A) vs (B) and see which restores non-vacuous coverage

qd3-which-lap.title: DECISION: whose time shares -- the driver's real lap or the constructor's ideal lap?
qd3-which-lap.imperative: Block on the counterpart. Decides whether the band width is driver-specific or a property of the ceiling.
qd3-which-lap.finding: ASKED: 'Time shares from the driver REAL lap (band width becomes driver-specific) or the constructor IDEAL lap (band width is a property of the ceiling, identical for team-mates)?' DECIDED (dispatch authorises): the driver's REAL lap (v_real). RATIONALE: the band's location is that class's own transit-time deficit, whose time base is where the real lap actually spent its seconds; scaling by the ideal lap's shares would mismatch the location it wraps. v_real is already in hand inside compute_class_utilization_observable, so no new input. RECORDED ALTERNATIVE: the ideal lap gives a driver-independent width, arguably more fitting for a session-level grip property -- if a later consumer needs team-mate-identical widths, this is the knob. @grade: guess . leans g2 . settle: compute per-class shares from v_real vs v_ideal on one weekend; if max |delta s_c| < 0.01 the choice is immaterial and can be frozen either way

qd4-api-shape.title: DECISION: replace ClassUtilizationObservable.g_sigma_onesided with a per-class array, or carry both session scalar and per-class array?
qd4-api-shape.imperative: Block on the counterpart. Weigh against the project's one-canonical-path tenet (no compatibility shims) versus the genuine distinctness of the two quantities.
qd4-api-shape.finding: ASKED: 'ClassUtilizationObservable.g_sigma_onesided is a float. Replace it with a per-class array, or carry both?' DECIDED (dispatch authorises): CARRY BOTH, as two named distinct quantities -- g_sigma_onesided_by_class: np.ndarray (shape (2+k), W-column order, the value the bands and the store rows take) and g_sigma_session_s: float (the session-level scale it was allocated from). This is NOT a compatibility shim (the project forbids those): the scalar is a genuinely different quantity that is separately consumed -- build_class_utilization_observables.py:476 logs it, and it is the right-hand side of the coherence identity sum_c sigma_c == sigma_session that the width-shape test asserts. One canonical path survives because there is exactly ONE way to obtain a per-class width. The old field NAME g_sigma_onesided is retired from the dataclass rather than silently re-pointed, so any missed caller fails loudly (AttributeError) instead of reading a scalar where an array is meant. The STORE column keeps its name g_sigma_onesided -- see qd5. @grade: settled/measured . leans g2,g3

qd5-format-version.title: DECISION: bump driver_class_observables format_version for the changed meaning of an existing column?
qd5-format-version.imperative: Block on the counterpart. The column keeps its name and type but changes meaning; existing rows would silently mix vintages.
qd5-format-version.finding: ASKED: 'The store column g_sigma_onesided keeps its name and type but changes MEANING (whole-lap sigma -> per-class sigma). Bump driver_class_observables format_version?' DECIDED (dispatch authorises): YES, bump it -- CONDITIONAL on a verification task first. RATIONALE: a store that mixes vintages would feed fit.py:247-257 a silent mixture of two semantics into sigma_cell, which is precisely the project's named 'silent wrong prediction / hidden fallback' failure mode; format_version is the existing, already-persisted mechanism for making a vintage legible, so nothing new is minted. NOT ASSUMED: the gate's first task greps every reader of format_version on driver_class_observables and confirms a bump neither breaks reads nor is silently ignored. FALLBACK if a bump would break reads or nothing gates on it: keep the version and instead update the store's schema comment (reference_utilization_store.py:78) plus a rebuild note, and say so explicitly rather than pretending the vintage is marked. @grade: guess . leans g3 . settle: grep readers of format_version on driver_class_observables -- if nothing gates on it the bump is free and purely documentary
